articles.title: Em alta na MPB, Jota.Pê faz um dos últimos shows da turnê em São Paulo | G1
articles.standfirst: Apresentação no Tokio Marine Hall acontece neste sábado (5), antes da estreia do novo projeto do cantor.
articles.summary: Apresentação no Tokio Marine Hall acontece neste sábado (5), antes da estreia do novo projeto do cantor.
articles.body:
Jota.Pê se apresenta em São Paulo. — Foto: Meneson Conceição / Divulgação

Para quem decidiu ficar em São Paulo no feriado prolongado do 7 de Setembro, uma das principais atrações da agenda cultural deste fim de semana é o show de Jota.Pê .

O cantor e compositor sobe ao palco do Tokio Marine Hall neste sábado (5), em uma apresentação que reúne os sucessos do álbum Se Meu Peito Fosse o Mundo e marca uma das últimas oportunidades de assistir a esse repertório ao vivo antes da chegada do novo trabalho do artista.

O show acontece em um momento especial da carreira de Jota.Pê. Desde o lançamento do álbum, em 2024, o músico se consolidou como um dos principais nomes da nova geração da MPB.

O disco conquistou três Grammys Latinos, incluindo o de Melhor Álbum de Música Popular Brasileira/Música Afro-Brasileira e o de Melhor Canção em Língua Portuguesa, com "Ouro Marrom" .

Ao longo de 2025, o artista ampliou ainda mais o alcance do trabalho. Integrando o projeto "Dominguinho" , ao lado dos músicos João Gomes e Mestrinho, voltou a conquistar um Grammy Latino e passou a ocupar espaço de destaque na cena musical brasileira.

Também foi premiado no Prêmio Multishow e eleito Artista do Ano pelo Prêmio Potências, reforçando o protagonismo que vem conquistando na MPB contemporânea.

No palco, Jota.Pê apresenta um repertório que mistura canções autorais, interpretações marcantes e uma sonoridade que transita entre a música popular brasileira, influências afro-brasileiras e ritmos nordestinos. Acompanhado de banda completa, o artista promete um espetáculo que alterna momentos intimistas e de celebração.

📅 Quando? 05 de setembro; abertura da casa às 19h; show, às 21h. 📍 Onde? Tokio Marine Hall | Rua Bragança Paulista, 1281 – Chácara Santo Antônio, Zona Sul de São Paulo. 💲 Quanto? A partir de R$ 160. ➡️Mais informações e ingressos

articles.title: Dinho manda recado a ministros e políticos antes de tocar 'Que país é este' no Rock in Rio  | G1
articles.standfirst: Vocalista do Capital Inicial fez discurso antes de cantar o clássico da Legião Urbana em show que homenageou os 30 anos da morte de Renato Russo.
articles.summary: Vocalista do Capital Inicial fez discurso antes de cantar o clássico da Legião Urbana em show que homenageou os 30 anos da morte de Renato Russo.
articles.body:
O vocalista do Capital Inicial, Dinho Ouro Preto, fez um discurso com críticas a ministros do Supremo Tribunal Federal ( STF ) e a políticos antes de cantar "Que País É Este?", clássico da Legião Urbana, durante o show da banda no Rock in Rio, na noite de sexta-feira (4). ( leia aqui a resenha crítica )

HORÁRIOS ROCK IN RIO: Confira a programação completa

"Essa próxima música aqui é para o Daniel Vorcaro, falou? Essa música aqui é para os ministros do STF, que nos devem explicações. Essa aqui é para os nossos políticos de direita, de centro e de esquerda, que nos devem explicações", afirmou o cantor.

Na sequência, Dinho disse acreditar na democracia brasileira. "A democracia brasileira vai sobreviver a isso. Nós, juntos, somos mais fortes", declarou.

Antes de iniciar a música, ele concluiu: "Isso aqui é para a distopia brasileira. Isso aqui se chama 'Que País É Este?'".

As críticas do vocalista acontecem em meio às investigação sobre supostas fraudes envolvendo o extinto Banco Master desencadeou uma das maiores crises políticas e institucionais de 2026 ao atingir o STF, a Polícia Federal, a Procuradoria-Geral da República e o Palácio do Planalto.

A divulgação de relatórios da PF pelo ministro André Mendonça expôs mensagens que apontam uma relação de proximidade entre o ministro Alexandre de Moraes e o ex-banqueiro Daniel Vorcaro, levando Moraes a negar irregularidades e pedir uma investigação contra o colega. ( Entenda a crise no STF )

O show marcou o encerramento do primeiro dia do Palco Sunset e reuniu o Capital Inicial e o guitarrista Dado Villa-Lobos em uma homenagem aos 30 anos da morte de Renato Russo e à trajetória da Legião Urbana.

A apresentação reuniu sucessos das duas bandas. Do Capital Inicial, o repertório incluiu "Quatro Vezes Você", "Independência", "Música Urbana", "Fátima", "Veraneio Vascaína" e "Natasha".

Dinho Ouro Preto se apresenta com Capital Inicial e Dado Villa-Lobos no Rock in Rio — Foto: Anderson Bordê/AgNews

Em homenagem à Legião Urbana, Dinho dividiu o palco com Dado Villa-Lobos para interpretar "Será", "Geração Coca-Cola", "Quase Sem Querer", "Tempo Perdido" e "Que País É Este?".

Embora a Legião Urbana nunca tenha se apresentado no Rock in Rio com Renato Russo, o festival realizou, em 2011, um Concerto Sinfônico em homenagem à banda no Palco Mundo.

O show desta sexta-feira marcou a décima apresentação do Capital Inicial no Rock in Rio, colocando a banda entre as artistas que mais vezes participaram do festival.

articles.title: João Victor Gonçalves, de Quem Ama Cuida, denuncia homofobia no RIR | G1
articles.standfirst: João Victor Gonçalves foi seguido por GH e amigos, que fizeram comentários e debocharam de sua roupa. Após a repercussão do vídeo, o streamer pediu desculpas e disse que fazia apenas 'entretenimento' na rua.
articles.summary: João Victor Gonçalves, o Mau Mau de Quem Ama Cuida, foi seguido pelo streamer GH Rell RJ no Rock in Rio e denunciou comentários homofóbicos feitos durante live.
articles.body:
João Victor Gonçalves, que interpreta Mau Mau em “Quem Ama Cuida”, acusou o streamer GH de homofobia após ser abordado no entorno do Rock in Rio. — Foto: Globo/Bob Paulino

O ator João Victor Gonçalves, que interpreta Mau Mau na novela “Quem Ama Cuida”, acusou um streamer de homofobia após ser abordado durante o Rock in Rio, na noite desta sexta-feira (4).

O episódio aconteceu no entorno da Cidade do Rock, no Rio de Janeiro, e foi transmitido ao vivo pela plataforma Kick, concorrente da Twitch.

Na transmissão, o streamer GH Rell RJ aparece acompanhado de amigos enquanto se aproxima do ator. Em determinado momento, eles fazem comentários sobre a roupa usada por João Victor. “Caralho, que é isso. Cara horroroso. Cara meteu um tomate”, dizem.

O grupo ainda aparece seguindo o ator por alguns segundos.

O trecho da transmissão foi posteriormente recortado e publicado nas redes sociais, onde passou a circular com críticas à "abordagem". Durante a live, não fica claro se o streamer e os amigos sabiam que o homem era o artista João Victor Gonçalves.

O g1 procurou o streamer GH e a plataforma Kick para esclarecer o episódio e saber quais são as políticas em relação a abordagens e comportamentos como os registrados na transmissão. Até a última atualização desta reportagem, não houve retorno de nenhuma das partes.

Após a repercussão do vídeo, o ator se manifestou nas redes sociais e classificou o episódio como homofobia.

“Somos mais fortes que qualquer coisa... Impunes não vão ficar, homofobia é crime. Isso é um retrato. Meu medo de ser roubado era maior. Homofobia não é entretenimento”, disse emocionado.

João Victor traçou ainda um paralelo entre o que viveu e a história de seu personagem em “Quem Ama Cuida”. Na trama, Mau Mau é um jovem em processo de descoberta da própria sexualidade que enfrenta a homofobia dentro de casa, principalmente nas relações com o avô, Otoniel (Tony Ramos).

Em seus stories, o ator afirmou que o episódio no Rock in Rio era “o retrato de tudo que a gente mostra” na novela.

“O Mau Mau é um personagem forte, valente, que encara essa homofobia estrutural que vive dentro de casa de uma forma muito corajosa. Ele engole e segue”, escreveu.

GH Rell RJ também se pronunciou sobre o episódio e afirmou que costuma fazer transmissões com abordagens e situações inusitadas nas ruas.

Segundo ele, o trecho foi retirado do contexto da live e acabou gerando uma onda de críticas nas redes sociais.

“Tava numa live aqui, mano, e eu fico fazendo um monte de entretenimento no meio da rua, tipo doideira com maluquice. Tava fazendo entretenimento com um cara que tava passando na rua e me dei mal. Sabe por quê? Cliparam, postaram lá no Twitter e eu tô recebendo um monte de hate. Se eu errei, eu peço desculpas porque nós é ser humano e nós erra”, afirmou.

A repercussão também provocou manifestações de colegas de elenco de João Victor em “Quem Ama Cuida”. Pedro Alves, que interpreta Fernando na novela, publicou uma mensagem em defesa do ator.

“Aquilo foi baixo, covarde e cruel. Aquilo não é brincadeira. Só quem sofre pode entender. Vergonha de ver que falhamos como sociedade", escreveu.

articles.summary: As apresentações ocorrem neste sábado (5), domingo (6) e segunda-feira (7), no Teatro Dom Bosco, com coral, orquestra, violoncelo, percussão e Libras.
articles.body:
Mais de 150 alunos sobem ao palco para o festival — Foto: Divulgação

Mais de 150 alunos de diferentes regiões de Campo Grande vão subir ao palco do Teatro Dom Bosco neste fim de semana para apresentar o resultado de um projeto de formação musical gratuita. O evento terá apresentações de coral, orquestra, violoncelo, percussão e Libras.

O Festival Compondo Talentos ocorre neste sábado (5), domingo (6) e segunda-feira (7), com apresentações de coral, orquestra, violão, violoncelo, percussão e até música acompanhada por Libras. A entrada é gratuita.

As apresentações começam às 18h30 no sábado e no domingo. Na segunda-feira, o festival começa às 18h. O Teatro Dom Bosco fica na Avenida Mato Grosso, 225, no Centro de Campo Grande.

O festival marca o encerramento do ciclo de formação do projeto, que reuniu 12 turmas ligadas a escolas, instituições e projetos sociais da capital. Durante as atividades, os participantes tiveram contato com diferentes linguagens musicais, incluindo canto coral, violão, violoncelo, percussão, banda, orquestra e Libras.

A proposta é levar ao palco um trabalho desenvolvido ao longo dos meses em diferentes pontos da cidade. O presidente do Instituto Cerrado Central, Daniel Escrivano, responsável pela realização do projeto, destaca a importância da iniciativa:

“Todo talento começa com a oportunidade de experimentar, aprender e ser ouvido.”

A programação foi dividida em três noites, com grupos diferentes em cada apresentação. Confira a programação completa;

Grupo de violão durante os ensaios — Foto: Divulgação

O primeiro dia de apresentações reúne corais, orquestras e turmas que destacam a diversidade musical do projeto. Encerrando a noite, a Orquestra Indígena, desenvolvida na Aldeia Urbana Darcy Ribeiro, combina música de concerto com cantos tradicionais e elementos das culturas indígena e brasileira:

Canto coral da Escola Municipal Dr. Tertuliano Meireles

Violoncelo da Orquestra Sinfônica Municipal de Campo Grande

Orquestra Indígena, da Fundação Ueze Zahran

A programação do segundo dia traz uma mistura de vozes, inclusão e ritmos afro-brasileiros, destacando a transformação social por meio da arte:

Canto coral do Lar do Pequeno Assis e da Associação Escola de Mãe Luz, com uma apresentação que integra a Língua Brasileira de Sinais (Libras) ao canto

Grupo de percussão Bojomalê, com uma performance marcada por percussão corporal, ritmos afro-brasileiros e maracatu

Orquestra Fraternidade Sem Fronteiras, projeto que oferece formação musical gratuita para crianças e adolescentes de 7 a 17 anos em situação de vulnerabilidade

No feriado da Independência, o encerramento do festival celebra a união de diferentes instrumentos, vozes e talentos da região:

Grupo de violão da Igreja Batista Popular

Grupo de música do Instituto Misericórdia

Projeto Madeiras Dedilhadas, da Universidade Federal de Mato Grosso do Sul (UFMS), responsável pelo show de encerramento

O festival é o resultado de um projeto de formação musical gratuita — Foto: Divulgação

Horário: 18h30 nos dias 5 e 6; 18h no dia 7

Local: Teatro Dom Bosco – Avenida Mato Grosso, 225, Centro, Campo Grande

articles.title: Dolly Parton’s sister reacts to ‘insensitivity’ from strangers after the ‘Jolene' singer passed away
articles.summary: Stella Parton expresses the family's grief over Dolly Parton's death, addressing insensitivity from strangers and calling for compassion and respect in her remembrance.
articles.body: Dolly Parton’s sister, Stella Parton, opened up about how the family has been dealing with the singer’s demise. She also warned everyone against making inconsiderate comments. Sharing that she has faced a lot of “insensitivity from strangers” after her sister left for her heavenly abode, Stella detailed how the Parton family is taking on all of the challenges altogether.Stella Parton opens up about how she has been dealing with things after Dolly Parton’s demiseThe 77-year-old singer-songwriter recently shared an Instagram post detailing how many people posted insensitive comments after her sister, Dolly Parton's, passed away. She expressed her gratitude for the people who have been wishing well for the family and actually showed up.She wrote, “First let me say, thank you to the ones of you who have shown ‘genuine’ support and love during this time of our family bereavement. We will be okay in time, but each of us will grieve in our own personal way. Every human being experiences pain and loss in life, and my family is no different.”She further added, “Sadly, because of the way our lives have been lived in front of the public, we have no choice but to be subjected to incredible pressure and insensitivity from strangers.”Stella Parton asks people to make a change in their lives and get inspired by Dolly PartonFurther down the post, she finally shared that people need to learn some compassion in their everyday life. She wrote. “Finally, I ask that you show more compassion and wisdom as we move forward in life. Use my sister’s life as an example for tolerance and respect toward others. It’s not about the most clever comments, fake AI garbage, or snarky tweets.”She concluded her post by adding, “That being said, I’ve always embraced my own personality and will continue to be myself and express my opinions as I deem appropriate regardless of what anyone thinks of me. It’s my right as a human being! Have a happy and safe weekend.”Dolly Parton passed away on August 25 after battling cancer. The singer had not revealed her health issues until after her passing. A statement from her representatives shared with PEOPLE revealed that the iconic star had left for her heavenly abode while she was admitted to a cancer facility, surrounded by family and loved ones. articles.title: Taapsee Pannu CALLS OUT Bollywood's obsession with 'same actors': 'All the rom-coms, glam stuff looks the same'
articles.summary: Taapsee Pannu has never shied away from calling out patterns she sees in the film industry. In her latest chat, she took aim at something many viewers.
articles.body: Taapsee Pannu has never shied away from calling out patterns she sees in the film industry. In her latest chat, she took aim at something many viewers have quietly noticed too: Bollywood films starting to feel repetitive because the same faces keep showing up in the same kind of stories. The actor, known for choosing offbeat and gritty roles, spoke candidly about how typecasting isn't just an actor's problem but a casting problem that filmmakers need to fix.Same actors, same genres, says Taapsee PannuSpeaking to Hindustan Times, Taapsee Pannu pointed out that Bollywood keeps recycling a small pool of actors for particular genres, which she believes is the real reason so many films end up looking alike. According to her, when studios rely on the same handful of stars for romance or glamour and another fixed set for thrillers, originality naturally takes a hit.She explained, "All the rom-coms, glam stuff looks the same because there are only those four or five actors, actresses who are doing that. All our thrillers look and feel the same because there are only those four or five actors who are doing that."She added that true novelty on screen requires filmmakers to be bolder with their choices. She said, "If you really want your film to look different, something new, something different, then you need to cast people who can bring that difference on screen."Costume changes don't erase the old image, says Taapsee PannuTaapsee Pannu also touched on how simply changing an actor's look or outfit doesn't automatically make a role feel fresh, since audiences already carry a fixed impression of that performer. She said, "If I've seen someone in a glamorous role, now you make that person wear a sari or a bikini or whatever, I have seen the glamour of that actor. It's only different, right?” she said, adding, “So that's not the fault of that poor actor, also."Taapsee Pannu on being typecast herselfTurning to her own journey, Taapsee Pannu acknowledged that she too has become synonymous with intense, hard-hitting characters, largely because those are the scripts she keeps receiving. She reasoned that picking the strongest script from a limited set only reinforces the label further. She said, "If you only offer me 10 intense films, I will choose the best out of them and present that, but it will still be a strong woman, intense film because that's the only genre that people have started imagining me."More about Taapsee Pannu's upcoming film 'Gandhari'Taapsee's remarks come alongside the release of her latest film, 'Gandhari', directed by Devashish Makhija and written and produced by Kanika Dhillon. She plays Bani, a mother whose life turns upside down after her daughter is kidnapped, pushing her into the eerie town of Joypurra and its unsettling Behrupiya lore. Ishwak Singh, Jatin Sarna, Swastika Mukherjee, Mita Vashisht, and Chhaya Kadam also star. The film began streaming on Netflix on September 3.Give your child the gift of confidence! articles.title: Kylie Jenner shows off sculpted figure as she shares secret behind toned body
articles.summary: Kylie Jenner looked incredible in a micro sports bra and capri leggings as she posed in the ALO gym ahead of her Reformer Pilates workout
articles.body:
Kylie Jenner recently shared a glimpse of her Reformer Pilates workout routine on Instagram, showcasing her sculpted physique and partnership with ALO gym.

The beauty mogul has been announced as ALO's newest ambassador, emphasizing the importance of self-care and finding moments of stillness in her life.

Reformer Pilates, a workout routine that combines high-intensity exercises with strength training and pilates, is a favorite of Kylie Jenner for targeting specific areas of the body and providing a challenging workout using resistance springs.

Kylie Jenner has just jumped on the Reformer Pilates hype – and, by the looks of it, the workout is delivering her sculpted results.

The beauty mogul took to her Instagram Stories on September 4 to share a glimpse inside her fitness routine. The photo captured Kylie straddling a Reformer bed located in the ALO gym as she posed for a mirror selfie. The star wore a black sports bra with a pair of matching, high-waisted capri pants. Her luscious locks were left down in soft waves and she opted for a makeup-free complexion.

"Waiting for my friends @haileybieber @laurenperez," Kylie penned alongside the image.

Kylie's choice of gym comes as no surprise considering she was recently announced as ALO's newest ambassador. "Some of the most meaningful parts of my life happen when no one's watching. Those moments of stillness are what help me feel grounded and present, and I've learned to protect them. That's what I love about this campaign – it reminds us that taking care of yourself starts with making space for the things that are yours alone," said Kylie in the campaign video.

The star previously collaborated with ALO for a Pilates voyage aboard a yacht in Sardinia back in June. The 29-year-old wore the signature Airlift Intrigue Bra that, according to the brand, has "a supportive, snug fit that's ready for everything from HIIT to headstands." The top was styled with the matching 3" Softsculpt Low-Rise Foldover Short, which are crafted from their "signature medium-compression fabric" to "sculpt and smooth while allowing you the freedom to move."

Reformer Pilates is the perfect workout routine for Kylie as she enjoys combining high-intensity exercises with strength training and pilates. Reformer Pilates uses an apparatus made up of pulleys and springs to work the body, using the resistance of the springs to feel the burn.

"Reformer Pilates often involves many of the same stretches as mat Pilates, but the beauty of the reformer is that it helps you to get more out of your workout and target particular areas of the body," Martyn Oakley, head of fitness at Everlast Gyms, previously explained to HELLO!

The reformer apparatus was designed by Joseph Pilates and consists of a rectangular, bed-like frame with a padded platform on runners known as a carriage (think a rowing machine mixed with a bed). At one end of the bed are the foot bar and springs which can be tightened to increase the resistance of the exercise. At the opposite end are two ropes with handles attached to pulleys which can be used by either hands or feet.

As for her diet, in an interview with Harper's Bazaar , Kylie revealed that she preferred to start her day with a meal of bone broth, celery juice, a vanilla iced latte and tea. She is also a fan of snacking and loves In-N-Out Burger. She avoids late-night cravings by snacking on apple slices before bed, and likes to research workouts "on the floor of my bedroom" rather than go to the gym.

articles.title: VHP bars Muslims from garba, dandiya events in Maharashtra; issues Aadhaar, tilak guidelines
articles.summary: MUMBAI: The Vishva Hindu Parishad (VHP) has said Muslims will not be allowed to participate in garba and dandiya events across Maharashtra during next.
articles.body: MUMBAI: The Vishva Hindu Parishad (VHP) has said Muslims will not be allowed to participate in garba and dandiya events across Maharashtra during next month’s Navratri festival and has issued guidelines asking organisers to verify participants’ Hindu identity.The measures suggested by the organisation include checking Aadhaar cards and applying tilak on the foreheads of attendees when Navratri begins on October 11.VHP spokesperson and joint secretary Shriraj Nair said the organisation had decided to prevent Muslims from taking part in garba and dandiya events during the festival, news agency PTI reported."We have taken a decision of not allowing participation of Muslims in garba-dandiya dance during the Navratri festival," Nair said."Navratri is not just about songs and dance. The festival is about worshipping the Goddess. Why should Muslims, who are against idol worship, participate in the festival?" he said.VHP issues guidelines for garba, dandiya organisersThe VHP has also issued guidelines for organisers, including checking Aadhaar cards of attendees and applying tilak as measures to verify their Hindu identity.Nair said the restrictions were not aimed at any particular community and described them as precautionary steps intended to preserve what the organisation considers the cultural character of Hindu festivals."The VHP, which is unwilling to compromise on its core agenda of religious conversion and anti-cow slaughter, believes festivals are an integral part of the cultural legacy of the Hindus. And it cannot allow its dilution. However, it admits the restrictions are precautionary measures and not directed against Muslims or any other communities," he said.VHP refuses to comment on Bhagwat remarksNair’s remarks came days after RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat, while addressing a gathering at Madison Square in New York, spoke about universal oneness and dignity for all people."If any Hindu thinks there should be no Muslims in India, he will not remain Hindu. If you want to call yourself a Hindu, you have to believe that all paths are leading to the same goal. Every human has dignity. There is no difference between human beings," Bhagwat had said.Asked about Bhagwat’s remarks, Nair said the VHP would not comment on the RSS chief’s statement."We are not against anybody. We also believe in social harmony and peace," he said.Nair, however, questioned why the VHP should ease its guidelines for Muslims whom he said did not subscribe to the religious beliefs and form of worship associated with Navratri."The point is, why should we relax our guidelines for Muslims who don't subscribe to our religious beliefs and style of worship?" he said."If Muslims are keen to participate in the Navratri festivities, they should come with their family members, wives and sisters. articles.title: Robotaxis enter their villain era
articles.summary: Road Rage is a new short film in production that casts a murderous autonomous car as the bad guy — and taps into everything people already fear about AI on the road.
articles.body: It’s Bullitt meets Christine meets Waymo. A new short film imagines a San Francisco car chase where the other driver isn’t human — and the car may be trying to kill you. That a robotaxi can now be cast as the villain with almost no explanation says something about the present moment. Autonomous cars have gone from sci-fi curiosities to fixtures in some American cities, where they’ve become stand-ins for anxieties about AI job displacement, Big Tech surveillance, and machines making decisions once left to humans. Road Rage, the planned short film awaiting $40,000 on Kickstarter to fund production, leans into all of it. The film pits Joa, a ridehail driver in a manual-transmission car, against Roboride, an autonomous vehicle that takes a minor road-rage incident very personally, according to a synopsis by its director, Romain Thomassin. Roboride lightly clips Joa’s mirror. Joa gives it the finger. The car decides to kill him. “It’s analog versus artificial,” Thomassin told The Verge. [Media: The AI bad guy will be played by an old Prius transformed with cold LED lights across the front — à la Tesla — fake cameras, a spinning lidar-like device on the roof, a black exterior, and a menacing, ever-blinking red dot. Thomassin calls the intended result a “nasty Waymo.” “I really wanted to play the nasty, gritty look of the ’70s car chase, but with today’s robotaxi in today’s San Francisco,” he said. The chase itself will be a throwback: real cars, real actors, and real stunts. "“I really wanted to play the nasty, gritty look of the ’70s car chase, but with today’s robotaxi in today’s San Francisco.”" - Road Rage director Romain Thomassin “What makes Joa the good guy is not only his instinct but also his authenticity,” Thomassin said, noting a scene in which the character has an unexpected conversation with his passengers. “This type of human interaction doesn’t happen in a robotaxi.” Thomassin doesn’t actually think robotaxis are inherently evil. But as a movie villain, they come preloaded with tension. For one thing, they’re replacing the kind of worker his protagonist represents. Joa is a Mexican immigrant trying to make a living driving in an increasingly expensive San Francisco. Robotaxis are already competing with ridehail drivers, just as generative AI is competing with workers in Thomassin’s own industry. “Driving here is a metaphor for what’s happening in cinema, in filmmaking,” Thomassin said. [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: Then there’s surveillance. Autonomous cars are covered in cameras and sensors, constantly observing the streets — and people — around them. That, more than the prospect of being driven around without a human behind the wheel, is what actually unnerves Thomassin. In Road Rage, that anxiety is pushed toward dystopia. There’s a brief encounter involving immigration enforcement, and Thomassin imagines a feature-length version in which autonomous cars identify people, trap passengers inside, or deliver them directly to authorities. The progression, as he describes it, is observation, surveillance, then control. “The next step is that [autonomous vehicles] could become the police,” he said. And because robotaxis operate as connected fleets, the threat can scale beyond one vehicle. “Imagine an army rising up,” Thomassin said. Robotaxis also make unusually good revenge-movie villains because people already treat them like adversaries. Thomassin points to the indignities Waymos have endured on San Francisco streets: people immobilizing them with traffic cones, tagging and vandalizing them, and even setting them on fire. “They are being bullied,” he said. In Road Rage, that mistreatment becomes the motivation: “They want to take revenge.” Thomassin describes Roboride as absorbing the behavior it observes around it — including the behavior of human drivers. The car is simply learning road rage from humans. “Humans are known to be the worst versions of themselves on the road,” he said. That makes Roboride a very 2026 update to the killer car idea in Stephen King’s Christine. There, the menace is supernatural. Here, it comes from something more contemporary: a machine that watches humans, learns from them, and inherits some of their worst traits along with the useful ones. On the other side of the chase is Joa and his stick shift — a deliberately analog counterpoint. To Thomassin, driving stick is a deeply human act: The driver remains in control of the vehicle, physically responding to the road. What separates Joa from Roboride, in Thomassin’s telling, is instinct — and even irrationality. During one confrontation, Joa takes his hands off the steering wheel while facing down the autonomous car. The move is so reckless that Roboride backs off. The human wins by becoming less predictable than the machine. "“Respect your madness. Be a little mad and creative in your way of doing things, and you will be able to rise against the machines.”" - Romain Thomassin “Respect your madness,” Thomassin said. “Be a little mad and creative in your way of doing things, and you will be able to rise against the machines.” Despite its skepticism toward AI, Road Rage may use some of the technology itself. Thomassin says the filmmakers are considering AI-generated imagery to depict what Roboride sees, while shooting the human driver’s world with traditional cinematography. To him, that distinction matters. He sees AI as a creative tool when it serves the story, rather than simply a way to replace workers. For all the menace he sees in robotaxis, Thomassin isn’t afraid to ride in them. He signed up for Waymo as soon as he could and uses it when visiting friends and family for rides. “I don’t feel in danger,” he said. That may be what makes Roboride such an effective 2026 villain. The scary part isn’t necessarily that the machine will crash. The scary part is that the machine works.

articles.title: Prince Harry, Meghan Markle accused of seeking ‘best of both worlds’ with UK move: expert
articles.summary: Prince Harry and Meghan Markle's U.K. return mirrors the "half-in half-out" arrangement Queen Elizabeth rejected, a royal expert says.

The Duke and Duchess of Sussex — who are reportedly looking for a home in Britain — are expected to maintain their ties to Montecito, California, while keeping their businesses based in the United States. Royal commentator Kinsey Schofield told Fox News Digital that the reported arrangement appears to give the couple access to Britain and the royal family while allowing them to maintain their independent lives in the U.S. "I suspect they want the best of both worlds — access to Britain, proximity to the monarchy and the credibility that comes with Harry’s royal identity, while maintaining the freedom and commercial opportunities they associate with life outside the U.K.," Schofield said. articles.body: Punjabi singer Parmish Verma has been ruling social media for quite some time now. Usually that happens because of his music, a virtual home tour or his upcoming projects. articles.title: De Hannah Montana, pasando por Miley Cyrus y ahora vuelve a modificar su nombre artístico
articles.standfirst: La artista decide llamarse simplemente Miley, elimina Cyrus y su padre reacciona a ello
articles.summary: La artista decide llamarse simplemente Miley, elimina Cyrus y su padre reacciona a ello
articles.body: Miley Cyrus anunció por sorpresa su nuevo álbum, cuyo título lleva 'Bass Persuades', y saldrá a la luz el próximo 18 de septiembre. Lo presentará en dos conciertos en el Hollywood Bowl durante el mes de octubre, algo que supone su vuelta a los escenarios tras años alejada de ellos. Pero este nuevo anuncio ha dejado un detalle curioso que no ha pasado inadvertido. Su nombre. Más en concreto. Su nuevo nombre. La estrella de Disney se ha quitado su apellido, para simplemente pasar a llamarse Miley. Y lo ha hecho por una razón familiar. De los primeros que han reaccionado a esta maniobra de la artista ha sido precisamente su padre, Billy Ray Cyrus, que ha reaccionado al respecto en sus redes sociales. "La familia significa más que nunca ahora. Siempre llamé a mi pequeña Miley. Simplemente... Miley. Igual que siempre llamé a mi hijito Braison", comenzó el artista de country en su texto. "Apuesto a que no lo sabías… Yo era simplemente Cyrus antes de que saliera Achy Breaky Heart en el 92. Toda mi ropa y camisetas solo decían: 'Cyruslo dio todo' con una imagen de una bandera de POWMIA y la frase: 'No te olvidamos", añadía su padre. De hecho, su padre reaccionaba con naturalidad a tal efecto. "Ayer le dije a Miley que me parecía bien que usara su nombre de pila. Mencioné a Dolly y Cher. Lo pienso cada vez más… Elvis… Prince… y así sucesivamente. Es una progresión natural para una leyenda superestrella icónica". Billy Ray eludió que haya polémica con el tema en cuestión, dejando claro que no hay tensión entre ellos, ya que hace años estuvieron distanciados por la tensa separación de este con Tish, madre de la cantante, en 2022 y las dinámicas familiares acumuladas desde la época de Hannah Montana. El paso de Hannah Montana a Miley Cyrus fue una transformación profunda y rebelde con la que la artista dejó atrás su etapa en Disney Channel para construir su propia identidad musical y personal. Un cambio radical. Su momento. de la infancia a la juventud. Nuevos ritmos. Nuevos objetivos. Miley protagonizó la exitosa serie de Disney Channel durante cuatro temporadas entre 2006 y 2011. Si bien el personaje utilizaba su nombre real y mezclaba la realidad con la ficción como estrategia comercial, la cantante sentía que su imagen aniñada le había sido impuesta y necesitaba conocerse a sí misma. De ahí ese primer cambio. Y ahora llega el siguiente paso en esa fase que entiende la artista alusivo a su evolución en la vida.

articles.title: Box Office Comeback: How Summer 2026 offers a glimmer of hope for Hollywood in the post-COVID era
articles.summary: The summer box office has generated over $4.5 billion, with "Spider-Man: Brand New Day" and "The Odyssey" shattering records at movie theaters.
articles.body: For much of the post-COVID era, it has been an uncertain time for Hollywood and movie theaters, but this summer offers a glimmer of hope for the entertainment industry. "I have to admit going into 2026, I didn't think that the theatrical model would rebound the way it has," film critic and podcast host Christian Toto told Fox News Digital. "We're seeing some of the summer movies just really overperforming in a dramatic way." The movie box office has generated over $4.5 billion this summer according to Box Office Mojo, the highest gross since 2019. 'THE DOG STARS' REVIEW: JACOB ELORDI FIGHTS FOR SURVIVAL IN RIDLEY SCOTT'S DULL POST-APOCALYPTIC WESTERN Blockbuster hits have been shattering records. "Spider-Man: Brand New Day," which continues to dominate at the box office grossing more than $860 million domestically and over $2.2 billion globally, has become the second-highest domestic grosser of all time and third-highest globally, while Christopher Nolan's "The Odyssey," has grossed more than $1.5 billion globally and is now the highest-grossing R-rated film of all time. Rotten Tomatoes box office columnist Erik Childress said the summer box office was packed with "everything," including original movies, small-budget features shattering expectations and top grossers like "Spider-Man." ‘MUTINY’ REVIEW: JASON STATHAM TAKES NO PRISONERS IN MINDLESS BUT AMUSING BRAWLER FLICK ON THE HIGH SEAS "There will always be sequels and franchises to lean on but theaters are filling up with people who want to see movies. We already have almost as many $100 million grossers (18) as we did last year (20) and there is likely another seven more in waiting this year to have the most we've seen since the pandemic and streaming gave everyone the Chicken Littles in their attitude toward the theatrical experience dying," Childress told Fox News Digital. "The box office is going to hit $9 billion for the first time since 2019 and maybe even get to the lauded $10 billion the industry has been chasing since before COVID hit." In addition to tentpole movies, low-budget horror films from young YouTubers have also defied gravity at the box office. Curry Barker's "Obsession," which defied odds by increasing its weekend grosses for multiple weeks, cracked over $500 million at the global box office, outpacing "The Mandalorian and Grogu," the latest big-budget "Star Wars" entry. And Kane Parsons' "Backrooms," made for a modest $10 million, grossed more than $81 million its opening weekend and went on to gross $390 million globally. ‘THE END OF OAK STREET’ REVIEW: ANNE HATHAWAY, EWAN MCGREGOR FIGHT DINOSAURS IN SURPRISINGLY FUN MOVIE Toto said movies like "Obsession" caught everyone off-guard. "It somehow connected with a younger audience and in a way that made them want to come back for more. It made them tell their friends. And I think that film was just really the sensation of the summer," Toto told Fox News Digital. The Hollywood in Toto founder said he's been encouraged by the box office results but stressed that Hollywood needs to continue the momentum by producing "compelling entertainment." "I think what this summer has shown is that if you put really compelling content out there, people will come," Toto said. "We love the 'Toy Story' movies, but you've got to put out an 'Obsession' now and then. You've got to put out something that people haven't seen before that says, 'Well, this speaks to me and my generation.' That matters." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

articles.title: Content creators drop the ball
articles.summary: Disruptions at the US Open and a controversial golf club ad are highlighting how influencers can be a liability for brands.
articles.body: During Naomi Osaka’s match against Anastasia Zakharova at this year’s US Open earlier this week, a gaggle of ring light-wielding influencers who were packed in a luxury suite became enough of a distraction that the umpire paused the match and repeatedly asked them to quiet down. Elsewhere in the USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center, other creators could be seen asking US Open staffers to take full-flash photos of them while Osaka and Zakharova were playing. Last month, United States Tennis Association (USTA) media operations director Jeanmarie Daly said that the US Open was “almost doubling” the number of content creators it was approving for credentials. There were “close to 100” influencers at this year’s tournament — up from 54 last year. But in a statement to ABC News, USTA spokesperson Brendan McIntyre emphasized that the influencers whose antics disrupted Osaka and Zakharova’s match were not credentialed by the organization. McIntyre also told The Athletic that media credentials were not given to Meg Radice and Audrey Jongens — two lifestyle influencers whose access to the US Open was revoked after they posted images of their badges to Instagram. According to McIntyre, Radice and Jongens “were improperly submitted for credentials on a staff list provided by a food vendor,” and seems like the creators might have screwed themselves over by flexing for their followers. Though those creators weren’t exactly practicing proper US Open etiquette, they were doing their jobs (read: making content) with the single-minded focus that often makes their presence an annoyance to the people around them. These influencers were at the US Open to share the experience with their followers, and regardless of whether they were invited by the USTA directly or not, they were helping the organization advertise the event to an audience that might not have otherwise been paying attention. [Media: Influencers have become an integral part of the advertising industry, with US creator ad spend hitting $37 billion in 2025 and being projected to reach $44 billion by the end of this year. Companies are increasingly relying on content creators to market their products, but what happened at the US Open is a snapshot of how that reliance can lead to undesirable outcomes for everyone involved. Videos of the US Open disruptions have gone viral across social media and sparked a conversation about whether influencers are the best people to invite to exclusive functions. But the point many people seem to be glossing over is that influencers are usually only invited to events like the US Open, awards shows, and film premieres because a brand decided it was worth bringing them there. As irksome as creators can be when they take up too much public space, that kind of behavior is something the companies that hire them have to anticipate. And as reporter Jessica Schiffer notes, some brands have been scrambling to get ahead of any potential blowback by sending out “helpful reminders” on tennis etiquette. [Media: Before a rule change in 2024, the US Open was actually much more strict about requiring attendees to stay in their seats until breaks during the match when players switch sides of the court. Now attendees can get up whenever they want, and the event features designated spaces close to the tennis courts where people can move freely — something tournament director Stacey Allaster described as “an important addition to the fan experience at the US Open.“ The influencers at this year’s US Open might not have technically been breaking any rules, but they were having a negative impact on other attendees’ viewing experience. And in the days after videos of the influencers began spreading online, the USTA put up new signage outside stadiums asking spectators to “please refrain from using flash photography or other lighting.” Taking selfies and shooting videos are core elements of the content creation hustle, but brands working with influencers should have made clear that, during a tennis tournament, there are times when it’s best to just watch the matches. While the content creators might have been having fun, many of the people around them weren’t able to enjoy the match in peace. That kind of main character energy often is exactly what companies want because it’s what keeps influencers’ fans engaged. But brands have to understand that simply letting creators run wild isn’t always the best plan of action. Callaway Golf Company learned this the hard way last month after an ad produced by YouTube channel-turned-sports apparel company Good Good hit the internet and immediately sparked outrage. The video — a spoof of Curry Barker’s Obsession — features Good Good cofounder Garrett Clark grinning maniacally after shoving professional golfer Alexis Miestowski to the ground when she reaches for his Callaway-branded driver. Many saw the ad as being distasteful and making light of violence against women, which prompted Callaway to issue an apology and sever ties with Good Good. [Media: In a statement about the ad and subsequent backlash, Callaway CEO Chip Brewer said that “mistakes were made, and we are taking the matter very seriously.” Brewer also admitted that Callaway signed off on the video before it was posted, but he insisted that its content did not reflect the company’s values. Though Callaway was quick to take the ad down, the fact that it was approved in the first place is an issue in and of itself. Even if the ad hadn’t been misogynistic, it still wasn’t funny or a particularly good riff on Obsession, and a more responsible advertising head probably would have requested significant revisions. The video was very on-brand for Good Good — a company that targets the kind of young, bro-y men whose attention (and money) the golfing industry is very keen on capturing. As The Athletic points out, Good Good is just one of many influencer outfits, including Barstool Sports and No Laying Up, that have built successful partnerships with golf brands. Similar to the way that the brands who sent influencers to the US Open should have given them some behavioral direction, companies like Callaway have to be mindful about what it means to use “edgy” content creators as their ambassadors. Influencers who have built successful platforms tend to like having creative control over the content they make, but companies paying them for promotion have a personal responsibility to make sure that they’re not being represented by people acting foolishly.

articles.title: Serie A official line-ups: Inter vs. Napoli

articles.body:
Inter do not give John Stones his first start behind Lautaro Martinez and Francesco Pio Esposito, as Napoli look to Rasmus Hojlund and Antonio Vergara after losing Scott McTominay.

It kicks off at San Siro at 17.00 UK time (18.00 CEST).

MILAN, ITALY – JANUARY 11: Rasmus Hojlund of SSC Napoli heads the ball whilst under pressure from from Hakan Calhanoglu of FC Internazionale Milano during the Serie A match between FC Internazionale and SSC Napoli at Giuseppe Meazza Stadium on January 11, 2026 in Milan, Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images)

This was the Scudetto showdown for the last two seasons, with Napoli taking the title in 2025 and Inter last term, and both are also gearing up for the start of the Champions League.

The Nerazzurri won both Serie A tests so far with Monza and Cagliari, and are taking their time to break in some summer signings.

Andy Diouf is preferred to Luis Henrique, as Djed Spence is still working his way back to full fitness, with Curtis Jones on the bench.

Lautaro Martinez and Pio Esposito are the front two again, as Marcus Thuram is not at 100 per cent.

It was reported that John Stones would get his first start in defence, but instead he is rested, along with Hakan Calhanoglu.

MILAN, ITALY – APRIL 05: Lautaro Martinez of Inter celebrates scoring his team's first goal during the Serie A match between FC Internazionale and AS Roma at Giuseppe Meazza Stadium on April 05, 2026 in Milan, Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images)

Napoli have had a rough start to the campaign, as the injury crisis from last season seems to have carried on with new problems into this.

Giovane also required an operation for a sports hernia, with Alessandro Buongiorno and Luca Marianucci already long-term absentees.

COMO, ITALY – MAY 02: Kevin De Bruyne of SSC Napoli looks on during the Serie A match between Como 1907 and SSC Napoli at Giuseppe Sinigaglia Stadium on May 02, 2026 in Como, Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images)

Kevin De Bruyne made good impacts off the bench in the first two games, but is not fully fit, so Antonio Vergara steps into a deeper midfield role.

Hojlund is again flanked by Alisson Santos and Matteo Politano.

Napoli are unbeaten against Inter since the Supercoppa Italiana Final in January 2024, managing one win and four draws.

NAPLES, ITALY – AUGUST 30: Massimiliano Allegri, Manager of Napoli, looks on during the Serie A match between SSC Napoli and Como 1907 at Stadio Diego Armando Maradona on August 30, 2026 in Naples, Italy. (Photo by Francesco Pecoraro/Getty Images)

Napoli: Meret; Di Lorenzo, Rrahmani, Marin, Spinazzola; Anguissa, Lobotka, Vergara; Politano, Hojlund, Alisson Santos

articles.title: Fantasy Footballers’ Andy Holloway is a dedicated zero-inbox kinda guy
articles.summary: Andy Holloway, the cohost of the Fantasy Footballers podcast, keeps tabs to a minimum and doesn’t let email pile up.
articles.body: Andy Holloway cohosts the Fantasy Footballers podcast with his friends Jason Moore and Mike Wright. The show is one of the premier fantasy sports podcasts, netting over 2 million monthly listeners and numerous awards, including Best Sports Podcast from iHeartRadio and People’s Choice at the Podcast Awards four years in a row. Holloway’s goal has always been about bringing fantasy football to a wider audience, not just hardcore nerds. With the NFL season starting next week and fantasy drafts in full swing, now seemed like a great time to see how Holloway stays focused during what is probably the busiest part of the year for a serious fantasy football fan. What is one thing you wish you could change about your phone? I wish it was less intrusive in everyday life. No matter how much I customize things, I am still overwhelmed with notifications and messages and things that “seem” required. How many tabs do you have open right now? Just 2! I’m very much a tidy tab user and a zero-inbox type of guy. What is your favorite gadget you’ve ever owned? I truly love my Whoop! It helps me stay motivated and accountable, barely needs to be charged, and builds camaraderie with friends. I resisted for years, thinking it was dumb, but I love it. People told us we couldn’t bootstrap it, but working with my best friends on a project we loved was the most satisfying accomplishment. What do you do when you need to focus? articles.title: Dolly Parton’s sister slams ‘fake AI garbage’ flooding the internet since icon’s death
articles.summary: Dolly Parton’s sister has condemned the AI deepfakes circulating in the wake of the beloved American icon’s death.
articles.body: Dolly Parton’s sister has condemned the AI deepfakes circulating in the wake of the beloved American icon’s death. Stella Parton, 77, addressed the fake AI-generated images and videos being of her sister in a statement shared to Instagram Friday, where she also thanked fans for their “genuine” support. “Sadly, because of the way our lives have been lived in front of the public, we have no choice but to be subjected to incredible pressure and insensitivity from strangers,” she wrote. “There is a tremendous amount of AI and endless garbage being posted everyday and it’s been challenging to absorb and or ignore.” “As time passes, those who are in the business of exploiting the loss and tragedies of others on a daily basis will move on to the next stampede of endless misinformation,” she added. It marks Stella’s most extensive comments yet on the online reaction since the larger-than-life country singer died a little more than a week ago following a brief battle with cancer. She was 80. The younger Parton is a country singer and songwriter in her own right. Stella had several hit songs in the 1970s, including “I Want to Hold You in My Dreams Tonight,” which was released in 1975. She is one of the American icon’s 11 siblings. “We will be okay in time but each of us will grieve in our own personal way,” she wrote. “Every human being experiences pain and loss in life and my family is no different.” Stella Parton said that her “big sister Dolly would be surprised and delighted by the love her family and she has been shown during this time.” “She loved her fans and the public in general,” she wrote. “That is the reason she chose not to express her opinions on a lot of things like politics, religion and individuals in the public eye.” She asked fans to “show more compassion and wisdom as we move forward in life.” “Use my sister’s life as an example for tolerance and respect toward others,” she wrote. “It’s not about the most clever comments, fake AI garbage or snarky tweets.” “At the end of the day or the end of a life, how will you feel about yourself?”

articles.title: Miss America contestant reveals surprising day job as Massachusetts police officer
articles.summary: Ashlyn Mercier became the first police officer named Miss Massachusetts and now competes for the Miss America crown while serving her community.
articles.body: Ashlyn Mercier has spent her career wearing a badge. Now, she's hoping to wear one of the country's most coveted tiaras. The Westborough, Massachusetts, police officer is competing in Miss America. The final competition takes place Sept. 6 at the Palm Beach County Convention Center in West Palm Beach, Florida. Mercier is also the first police officer to be named Miss Massachusetts. "I think there's not one single look for what a female police officer is supposed to look like," Mercier told Fox News Digital. "And if we say that there is, that's just wrong because, at the end of the day, yes, female law enforcement officers only make up approximately 14% of the force in the United States, but we don't have to look a certain way." NAVY VETERAN TRADES MILITARY UNIFORM FOR MISS GEORGIA SASH FOLLOWING HEARTBREAKING LOSS "People are so multifaceted, women are so multifaceted, and I'm just trying to show young girls that they can chase all of their dreams simultaneously," Mercier said. "They don't have to pick one thing and make that their entire identity." The glitzy competition dates to a 1921 beauty contest in Atlantic City, New Jersey, held a year after the 19th Amendment guaranteed women the right to vote. The organization awards scholarships and gives its titleholder a national platform for community service and advocacy. Mercier hopes to raise awareness of her cause, "Nick's Courage: One Smile Goes a Mile," named after her younger brother, Nicholas, a two-time pediatric cancer survivor. The initiative aims to bring positivity and hope to children battling critical illnesses. In 2025, she took a year off from pageant competition to follow in her father's footsteps and attend the police academy. WATCH: ACTIVE-DUTY POLICE OFFICER COMPETES IN MISS AMERICA "I didn't know if I would ever come back and compete," Mercier said. "I was afraid of what other people would think if I chased both of those dreams at the same time. I also had this dream of becoming a police officer. But what I came to realize is that I can't worry about what other people think. I've got to focus on myself. And it ended up working out for me." Mercier said the Westborough Police Department has been cheering her on as she balances the competition with her work as an officer. Fox News Digital reached out to the department for comment. "I'm really fortunate that they have been so incredibly supportive," Mercier said. "I work for an amazing department, and my co-workers have supported me 100% from the moment I told them I was competing as Miss Massachusetts to now being at Miss America. They've shown up to my sendoff parties, they've helped me with my fundraising efforts, they've sent me good luck texts." "It's really just an honor to be surrounded by people who uplift me," she said. "It really continues to help motivate me to move forward." Mercier said her career in law enforcement doesn't give her an advantage on the Miss America stage. She's one of the delegates representing the 50 states, the District of Columbia and Puerto Rico, each hoping to stand out. Still, other officers have taken notice. "There are also young girls saying that they want to get into law enforcement, and they're inspired by my story. And then, I serve my community in Westborough every single day in my capacity as a police officer, but I also get to serve my community in the role as Miss Massachusetts." "Those two things are what is so important about the Miss America opportunity," Mercier said. "Yes, we get to dress up. Yes, we get to wear pretty gowns and look beautiful. But, women's empowerment and service are the core. And if you look at it like that, you can see and draw a lot of parallels between Miss America and between my role as Officer Mercier." articles.title: Trump pardons Jay-Z associate Emory Jones after federal drug conviction
articles.summary: Alice Marie Johnson revealed Trump granted clemency to 30 individuals, including Emory Jones, a Roc Nation executive and Jay-Z's longtime associate.
articles.body: Emory Jones, longtime friend and business associate of Jay-Z, has been granted a pardon by President Donald Trump. Jones, who is now an executive in Jay-Z's Roc Nation, was sentenced to nearly 16 years in 2000 on federal drug charges. Thanks in part to a letter from the hip-hop mogul, his sentence was reduced by 37 months, but now, Trump has given him a completely clean slate. The news was shared this week by Alice Marie Johnson, who was pardoned by Trump in 2020 after being sentenced to life in prison on a nonviolent drug charge in 1996. She now works with the White House as the "pardon czar." JELLY ROLL GRANTED PARDON BY TENNESSEE GOVERNOR IN CHRISTMAS SEASON CLEMENCY DECISION "Yesterday was a powerful day for second chances," Johnson wrote on Instagram. "I am deeply grateful to President @realdonaldtrump for granting clemency and pardons to 30 deserving individuals whose cases we carefully reviewed and brought forward—and to the White House Counsel team, led by Will Scharf, for the hard work behind these decisions." She added, "Among them is Emory Jones, who served nearly 16 years in federal prison and came home determined to build a different life. Today he is an entrepreneur and creative leader whose journey reminds us how much people can grow—and how much good they can still do." TODD CHRISLEY RECALLS EMOTIONAL PHONE CALL WITH DAUGHTER SAVANNAH AFTER CONTROVERSIAL TRUMP PARDON In 1999, Jones pleaded guilty to a charge of conspiracy to distribute cocaine. The following year, he was sentenced to 188 months, nearly 16 years, in prison, with five years supervised release. Jones' legal team submitted a request for a reduction of his sentence in 2009, and as part of their request, they submitted a series of letters from people familiar with Jones, including Jay-Z. In a letter to the judge, Jay-Z, whose real name is Shawn Carter, wrote that he'd be offering Jones an executive assistant job with Roc Apparel Group upon his release, with a starting salary of $50,000. articles.title: 'Shah Rukh Khan said I'm a Pathaan, just shoot me if you want,' Sanjay Gupta recalled how the superstar refused to bow down to underworld threats
articles.summary: Shah Rukh Khan’s rise to superstardom coincided with a period when Mumbai’s underworld had a strong and often intimidating presence in Bollywood. Acto.
articles.body: Shah Rukh Khan’s rise to superstardom coincided with a period when Mumbai’s underworld had a strong and often intimidating presence in Bollywood. Actors, filmmakers and producers were sometimes subjected to threats and pressure, and Shah Rukh too found himself on the radar of gangsters. Filmmaker Sanjay Gupta has now recalled how the actor refused to be intimidated and stood his ground despite the risks involved.Gupta said Shah Rukh responded to the threats in unusually defiant fashion. According to the filmmaker, the actor made it clear that he would not allow anyone to dictate the films or shows he worked on.He said on Hussain Zaidi's podcast, "The only guy in the film industry, Shah Rukh Khan, when he was threatened, he said, ‘I will never do the film or show, I am a Pathaan, just shoot me if you want’. I am not scared of you, but I will not work with you and not do shows for you. He actually earned their respect. They also must have felt that there’s at least one person…”Despite his bold stance, the threats were serious enough for Shah Rukh to remain under police and security protection for around three years.The actor had previously opened up about the dangers he faced during the 1990s in an interview with comedian and actor Ruby Wax. Recalling how the underworld allegedly operated, Shah Rukh explained the pressure stars could face when they refused to cooperate.“They would set up a system, and they would say you do it. I may not have succumbed to it, but then they shoot you. So, sometimes it’s nice to do a film,” he said.Wax then sought clarification, asking, “You’re seriously saying someone calls you and says be in my film or I’ll blow your head off?”Shah Rukh confirmed that the reality was even more disturbing than Wax’s description.“Not as nicely as you’re saying it.” When asked whether he had personally received death threats, the actor did not hesitate.“Oh yes, on many occasions… I had a lot of security for three years.Shah Rukh’s willingness to confront threats was also recalled by filmmaker Karan Johar in his autobiography An Unsuitable Boy. Johar described an incident in which he himself faced pressure from the underworld around the release of Kuch Kuch Hota Hai.According to Johar, Shah Rukh refused to let the situation intimidate either of them. He wrote, “Shah Rukh said, ‘What nonsense!’ He went inside and dragged me out. He said, ‘I’m standing here in front of you. Let’s see who shoots you. I’m standing right here.’”Johar further recalled Shah Rukh reassuring his mother and making it clear that he would stand by his friend.“I’m a Pathan. Nothing can happen to me and nothing will happen to your son. He’s like my brother. Nothing’s gonna happen.”The relationship between Mumbai’s film industry and the underworld was not a new phenomenon, but the nexus became increasingly visible during the late 1980s and 1990s. articles.title: CD sales are booming as physical media continues its resurgence
articles.summary: CD sales are booming, and vinyl continues its resurgence, but that doesn’t mean people are abandoning streaming.
articles.body: According to the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA), CD sales exploded in the first half of 2026. A new report from the organization says 17.5 million CDs were sold in the first six months of the year, up from just 12 million during the same period in 2025. That’s a jump of 45.7 percent, and 58.6 percent in dollars, which reached $171.1 million. What makes this all the more shocking is that CD sales actually shrank 22 percent from 2024 to 2025. The RIAA isn’t the only one to notice the boom in CD sales. In July, research firm Luminate released a report saying that 16.3 million units were sold in the first half of 2026. It suggested that much of that increase was due to special editions from K-Pop acts like BTS and that Gen Z and millennials were treating them mostly as collectibles, saying that only about half of buyers actually owned a CD player. Vinyl continued its resurgence as well, with the number of units sold climbing by nearly 21 percent from last year to 26.5 million. “Other physical” media, which includes CD singles, DVDs, cassettes, SACD, DVD-Audio… basically anything besides “standard vinyl and CD albums,” also surged by over 73 percent, to 1.6 million units. Despite the increased interest in physical media and the ongoing iPod revival, people are not leaving streaming in droves. Streaming revenue grew by 4.7 percent to $4.9 billion — dwarfing all physical media combined. [Image: Those are some big jumps in sales.

articles.title: Rick Moranis, Cameron Diaz and Lindsay Lohan among stars who left fame behind before returning to Hollywood
articles.summary: From Rick Moranis to Cameron Diaz and Lindsay Lohan, these Hollywood stars walked away from fame and made remarkable comebacks years later on screen.
articles.body: Rick Moranis is stepping back into the spotlight after decades away from Hollywood, joining a growing list of stars who left fame behind and later returned. The 71-year-old actor is taking on his first live-action part in nearly 30 years after walking away from the entertainment industry at the height of his career following a family tragedy. Now, Moranis is reprising his role as Lord Dark Helmet in "Spaceballs: The New One," the long-awaited sequel to Mel Brooks' 1987 cult classic science-fiction comedy movie "Spaceballs." 'DEADPOOL' STAR ROB DELANEY REVEALS HOW LOSING 2-YEAR-OLD SON CHANGED HIS APPROACH TO FAME In July, Moranis made a rare public appearance to promote the sequel at San Diego Comic-Con, where he received a standing ovation when he appeared on stage wearing his character's signature massive black helmet. Moranis participated in a panel discussion alongside co-stars Daphne Zuniga, Josh Gad, Keke Palmer and Lewis Pullman as well as director Josh Greenbaum and screenwriters Benji Samit and Dan Hernandez. Zuniga is reprising her role as Princess Vespa while other original stars who returned for the sequel include George Wyner as Colonel Sandurz, Bill Pullman as Lone Starr and Brooks as Yogurt. During the panel, Moranis revealed what finally brought him back in front of the camera after his decades-long hiatus. "This came along right at the right time, and I started talking to these folks and hearing who was going to be in it," Moranis said, via People. "I spoke to Josh Greenbaum and I heard that Bill Pullman was coming back and that Lewis was going to be in it too, and it just felt like this is it. It’s time and — yes. I said yes, and it is the best decision I’ve ever made." Moranis became one of Hollywood's most recognizable comedy stars in the 1980s and 1990s after starring in a string of hit movies including "Spaceballs," "Ghostbusters," "Little Shop of Horrors," "Honey, I Shrunk the Kids," "Parenthood," "My Blue Heaven" and "The Flintstones." However, after his wife, costume designer Ann Belsky, died in 1991 following a battle with breast cancer, Moranis stepped away from show business to focus on raising their two children, daughter Rachel and son Mitchell. He last appeared on-screen in 1997's "Honey, We Shrunk Ourselves," the third installment in the "Honey, I Shrunk the Kids" movie series. During a 2015 interview with the Hollywood Reporter, Moranis reflected on his decision to prioritize his family over his career. "I was working with really interesting people, wonderful people," he said. "I went from that to being at home with a couple of little kids, which is a very different lifestyle. But it was important to me. I have absolutely no regrets whatsoever. My life is wonderful." Moranis also clarified that he had not officially retired from acting, telling the outlet, "I took a break, which turned into a longer break." "But I’m interested in anything that I would find interesting," he continued. "I still get the occasional query about a film or television role and as soon as one comes along that piques my interest, I'll probably do it." MATT DAMON SAYS HOLLYWOOD'S 'RUTHLESS' NATURE HAS TAKEN HIM AWAY FROM FATHERHOOD MORE THAN HE'D LIKE "I’m happy with the things I said yes to, and I’m very happy with the many things I’ve said no to," Moranis added. "Yes, I am picky, and I’ll continue to be picky. Picky has worked for me." Though Moranis left live-action films behind for many years, he continued working occasionally as a voice actor. He first dipped his toe back into the movie business in 2001, voicing two characters in "Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer & the Island of Misfit Toys." Some of his other voice-acting gigs include "Brother Bear," "The Animated Adventures of Bob & Doug McKenzie," and the voice of Dark Helmet in "The Goldbergs." During his appearance at Comic-Con, Moranis once again set the record straight regarding the perception that he had retired as he revealed that he and Brooks had long discussed making a follow-up to "Spaceballs." "Actually, I started talking to Mel about the sequel in 1989," he said. "We kept talking about it." "I really wasn’t retired; I was just negotiating," Moranis joked. STOCKARD CHANNING HITS FIRST RED CARPET IN 2 YEARS AFTER SAYING SHE'S A 'RECLUSE' While Moranis’ return has drawn renewed attention due to his decades-long absence, other stars have also taken long breaks from Hollywood before making high-profile comebacks. Here's a look at several celebrities who stepped away from the spotlight for years before finding their way back to the screen. Cameron Diaz Cameron Diaz was one of Hollywood’s most bankable stars when she quietly stepped away from acting in 2014. Diaz made her breakthrough in 1994's "The Mask" and went on to star in a series of hit films including "There’s Something About Mary," "My Best Friend's Wedding," "Charlie's Angels," "My Sister's Keeper," "Shrek" and "The Other Woman," among others. After starring in 2014's "Annie," Diaz walked away from show business to focus on building a life with husband Benji Madden. "It felt like the right thing for me to reclaim my own life, and I just really didn't care about anything else," the actress said during a 2025 appearance at Fortune's Most Powerful Women Summit, according to E! News. "Nobody's opinion, nobody's success, no one's offer, no one's anything could change my mind about my decision of taking care of myself and building the life that I really wanted to have. I think it really comes to what are you passionate about? For me, it was to build my family." During her break, Diaz welcomed daughter Raddix, 6, and son Cardinal, 2, with Madden and launched her Avaline wine brand. The couple's third child, son Nautus, was born in May. After a decade away from movies, Diaz returned to the screen in Netflix’s 2025 action comedy "Back in Action," starring opposite Jamie Foxx. She has since lined up other projects including Netflix’s "Bad Day," Apple TV+’s "Outcome" and "Shrek 5," in which she will reprise her voice role as Princess Fiona. Lindsay Lohan Lindsay Lohan’s comeback followed years of intense public scrutiny and a long stretch away from major studio films. Lohan became one of Hollywood’s biggest young stars after breaking out in "The Parent Trap" and later leading hits including "Freaky Friday," "Mean Girls" and "Herbie: Fully Loaded." However, Lohan's promising career was derailed by multiple box-office flops and a string of highly-publicized legal problems and substance abuse issues. After years of tabloid attention and personal struggles, Lohan left the United States in 2014 and eventually relocated full-time to Dubai, spending much of the next decade outside the Hollywood spotlight. She told Emirates Woman in 2018 that moving to Dubai afforded her "a fresh start." Lohan began rebuilding her acting career with Netflix’s 2022 holiday movie "Falling for Christmas," followed by more streaming projects and a major return to one of her signature roles in "Freakier Friday." During a 2025 interview with The Sunday Times, Lohan said she stepped away because she had lost her excitement for making movies and wanted "a more private life, a real life," before returning once she felt "that itch again." Lohan will next be seen in Hulu’s "Count My Lies," a limited series in which she stars opposite Shailene Woodley and Kit Harington. Ke Huy Quan Ke Huy Quan’s Hollywood disappearance ended with one of the industry’s most celebrated comeback stories. Quan became a child star after playing Short Round opposite Harrison Ford in 1984’s "Indiana Jones and the Temple of Doom" and Data in 1985’s "The Goonies." However, Ke only landed a few minor TV and film roles after his early fame and found himself being offered stereotypical parts geared toward Asians. During a 2023 interview with People, Quan said that he made the "very difficult decision" to walk away from acting in the early 2000s. He then spent years working behind the camera as a stunt coordinator and assistant director. However, he recalled that after seeing 2018’s "Crazy Rich Asians", he was inspired to revisit his first love. LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS "I was happy working behind the camera, but I had serious FOMO (fear of missing out)," Ke told the outlet. "I wanted to be up there with my fellow Asian actors." After roughly two decades away from acting, Quan returned in 2022’s "Everything Everywhere All at Once," a role that earned him the Academy Award for best supporting actor. In his emotional Oscars speech, Quan reflected on his unlikely journey, saying, "Dreams are something you have to believe in. I almost gave up on mine." Daniel Day-Lewis Daniel Day-Lewis has stepped away from Hollywood more than once, but his latest return marked the end of what many believed was a permanent retirement. Known for his intensely selective approach to roles, Day-Lewis has previously taken long breaks throughout his career. After starring in 1997’s "The Boxer," Day-Lewis retreated from acting and spent several years in Italy learning shoemaking before returning in Martin Scorsese’s 2002 film "Gangs of New York." The three-time Oscar winner announced he was retiring from acting after starring in 2017’s "Phantom Thread." At the time, his representative said, "Daniel Day-Lewis will no longer be working as an actor. He is immensely grateful to all of his collaborators and audiences over the many years. This is a private decision and neither he nor his representatives will make any further comment on this subject." Eight years later, his son, Ronan Day-Lewis, persuaded him to co-write and star in the 2025 drama "Anemone." Day-Lewis later pushed back on the idea that he ever meant to permanently retire. In a 2025 Rolling Stone interview, Day-Lewis said he "never intended to retire, really," and called his earlier retirement announcement "grandiose gibberish." He explained that he still loved the work, but struggled with the lifestyle around filmmaking and felt "hollowed out" after "Phantom Thread." He said returning for "Anemone" was largely about working with Ronan, who directed the film. Day-Lewis said that collaboration brought the spark back, saying, "working with Ro, that furnace just lit up." Renée Zellweger Renée Zellweger stepped away from Hollywood after years of working at a relentless pace. Zellweger became one of the most prominent actresses of the late 1990s and 2000s with roles in the hit movies "Jerry Maguire," "Bridget Jones’s Diary," "Chicago," "Cold Mountain" and "Cinderella Man." But after 2010’s "My Own Love Song," Zellweger took a six-year break from acting. During a 2025 interview with British Vogue, Zellweger explained why she decided to pause her career. "I was sick of the sound of my own voice. When I was working, I was like, ‘Oh my gosh, listen to you. Are you sad again, Renée? Oh, is this your mad voice?’ It was a regurgitation of the same emotional experiences," she said. Zellweger told the outlet that her hiatus from acting enabled her to pursue other projects and embrace a healthier lifestyle. "I built a house, rescued a pair of older doggies, created a partnership that led to a production company, advocated for and fundraised with a sick friend, and spent a lot of time with family and godchildren and driving across the country with the dogs. I got healthy." Zellweger returned in 2016 with the hit sequel "Bridget Jones’s Baby." She went on to earn some of the strongest reviews of her career for playing Judy Garland in 2019’s "Judy" and her performance earned her the Academy Award for best actress. Zellweger previously won the best supporting actress Oscar for her performance in "Cold Mountain." Macaulay Culkin Macaulay Culkin walked away from Hollywood after becoming one of the most famous child stars in the world. Culkin shot to superstardom as Kevin McCallister in 1990’s "Home Alone" and its 1992 sequel, "Home Alone 2: Lost in New York." He went on to star in hit films including "My Girl," "The Good Son" and "Richie Rich." Pamela Anderson Pamela Anderson’s return to the spotlight has become one of Hollywood’s more unexpected late-career reinventions. Anderson became a global sex symbol in the 1990s through "Baywatch," Playboy and years of tabloid attention that often overshadowed her acting ambitions. articles.title: Spencer Pratt rips George Clooney's 'woke scold lecture' after Amal's lavish Venice look
articles.summary: Spencer Pratt calls out George Clooney and Amal Clooney over Venice Film Festival glamour, saying he will never tolerate a "woke scold lecture" from the couple.
articles.body: Spencer Pratt is taking aim at George Clooney. The former reality star, who delved into politics this year with a run for mayor of Los Angeles, pulled no punches when he took to social media Friday to criticize Clooney and his wife, Amal. "$500M net worth George Clooney could’ve permanently housed 8 homeless people for the rest of their lives with the money he spent on a single-use dress for his wife at a 4 hour event," Pratt claimed on X. SPENCER PRATT'S UNEXPECTED POLITICAL RISE FROM MTV VILLAIN TO KAREN BASS' CHALLENGER He added, "I will never tolerate a woke scold lecture from these people. Just be an ostentatious celebrity and own it." Along with his post, he shared a Page Six article detailing a look Amal wore to the Venice Film Festival, where the Clooneys have been spotted several times this week. According to the outlet, she wore a custom look by Haider Ackermann for Tom Ford, as well as a pair of earrings from Cartier that cost $149,000 and a Cartier diamond bracelet that runs for $225,000.
